# Personal and sensitive data

<!-- Generated by governance/build_docs.py from the data dictionary; do not edit. -->


Classification of Silver fields that hold personal or sensitive data, with the proposed Microsoft Purview sensitivity label and how each is protected. The same classification appears in [data_catalogue.md](data_catalogue.md).

| Class | Label | Protection |
|---|---|---|
| Personal: identity | Confidential - Personal | Shown to Head Office and Property Managers; hidden (OLS) for others |
| Personal: contact | Confidential - Personal | Masked on SQL endpoint; hidden (OLS) except Head Office, PMs |
| Personal: sensitive | Highly Confidential - Personal | Masked everywhere; reported only as counts (checked yes/no) |
| Personal: financial | Highly Confidential - Personal | Row-level security: a user sees only the tenancies they manage |
| Bank details | Highly Confidential - Financial | Masked on the SQL endpoint; never in the semantic model |
| Free text (may hold personal data) | Confidential - Personal | Not shown in reports; reviewed before any export |

## How the protection is applied

- **Sensitivity labels.** Apply the labels above in Microsoft Purview to `ll_silver`, `ll_gold` and the semantic model, so they follow the data into exports (Excel, PDF) and block unlabelled sharing.
- **Masking on the SQL endpoint.** Dynamic data masking on the Gold tables' contact and bank fields, e.g. `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN email ADD MASKED WITH (FUNCTION = 'email()')`; only roles granted `UNMASK` see real values.
- **Object-level security (OLS).** In the semantic model, tenant names, emails, mobiles and bank details are hidden from every role except Head Office and Property Manager.
- **Row-level security.** Tenancy balances and rent transactions are filtered to the homes a user manages (see [rls.md](rls.md)).
- **Lakehouse access.** Only data engineers can read `ll_bronze` and `ll_silver`; analysts and report users get `ll_gold` and the semantic model.
- **Retention.** Personal data of former tenants and unsuccessful applicants should be reviewed against the retention policy (e.g. 6 years after the tenancy ends) and removed in the source systems.
